<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours. One island. Not much else.</b><br>
  A lo-fi video of one young woman on one very small island, nodding to her headphones for ten hours.<br>
  Every so often something happens, always on the beat. Then she goes back to nodding.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <kbd>100</kbd> index &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <kbd>200</kbd> <a href="activities.toml">gags</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <kbd>300</kbd> <a href="tools/schedule.py">timers</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <kbd>400</kbd> weather &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <kbd>500</kbd> <a href="tools/make_audio.py">sound</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;

</p>

**Castaway** *(working title)* is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime scene. 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime. More than 90 activities live in [activities.toml](activities.toml), most of them on four timers, every one of them starts on the next bar of the music, and every sound is synthesized from code. Still in development, so nothing is on air yet. This page is what the service would look like if it were.

Press 700:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

The page in [web/index.html](web/index.html) plays a live preview and exports a YouTube-ready MP4: Chrome encodes every frame exactly with WebCodecs (H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30) and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.

<details>
<summary><b>P200 · Island gags</b>: all true, all on the beat</summary>
<br>

```text
 P200 RAFTEXT 200                              ISLAND GAGS, ON THE BEAT
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Crab moves out, wearing a coconut .................................. 201
 Bottle sent; the sea sends it back ................................. 202
 Drone delivers: more headphones .................................... 203
 Stray cat arrives on a crate, naps ................................. 204
 Shark in headphones nods along ..................................... 205
 Hydrofoil bro: shaka, carves off ................................... 206
 Walks out to sea. Back with coffee ................................. 207
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Every gag starts on the next bar of the music: one bar is 3 seconds.
```

- <kbd>201</kbd> A coconut falls on a hermit crab. The crab keeps it, and the coconut walks off with the crab inside. This one is in the banner, about 18 seconds in: the crab walks right past her feet. She is nodding. She misses it.
- <kbd>202</kbd> A message in a bottle washes straight back. Some time later a different bottle brings a reply.
- <kbd>203</kbd> A delivery drone drops a parcel. It is another pair of headphones.
- <kbd>204</kbd> A stray cat (grey tabby, white chest) arrives on a crate, climbs the palm and naps. One day it floats away again. Another day it comes back.
- <kbd>205</kbd> A shark in headphones surfaces and nods to the beat.
- <kbd>206</kbd> A bro on an electric hydrofoil waves with a shaka and carves off.
- <kbd>207</kbd> She could leave any time. Once in a long while, she does: she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee.

Also on the schedule: the signal hunt (one bar of signal, at the top of the palm), a sea turtle who visits, a tour boat of selfie-takers, and a ship that sails past exactly while she is busy with a coconut (it waits for her to get busy first). Bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing. A kumara, planted in the sand, that grows over the course of the video. And the everyday ones: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle that the tide takes, waving for rescue.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>P300 · Timers</b>: four of them, and a lot of calm in between</summary>
<br>

| Timer | Comes round every | In a 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| Occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| Rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| Super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 a run | about 2 |
| Chained | only after something else | about 20 |

Counts are the medians of 200 simulated runs, as the header of [activities.toml](activities.toml) gives them. The file held 94 activities on 1 October 2026 and gains more every few hours. Each timer picks by weight among the activities that are free right now. Lanes let things overlap: she has one lane, and the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, and the shore have their own, so the world carries on while she is busy. She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest. Every start snaps to the next bar of the 80 BPM theme, so the gags land on the beat.

```sh
python tools/schedule.py     # validate the file and simulate a 10-hour run
```

The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`: same seed, same video, event for event.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>P400 · Island weather</b>: sunny, then more sunny</summary>
<br>

```text
 P400 RAFTEXT 400                                        ISLAND WEATHER
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 TODAY      Sunny. Daytime.
 TONIGHT    Not scheduled. No night scenes, ever. It is a project rule.
 SEA        Calm. Shore waves and drifting cloud shadows: built.
 OUTLOOK    A rain shower is planned.
 LATER      Birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins,
            sailboats, sandpipers and a gecko: also planned.
```

Scene life runs on its own timers, underneath the routines. The forecast never changes: the project has a rule against night, so every hour of the run is the same lovely day.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>P500 · Sound</b>: all of it made in code, none of it heard yet</summary>
<br>

Every sound is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loop packs, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far.

- **Theme:** a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression, 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle.
- **Ocean:** a seamless 60-second loop of its own.
- **Mix:** -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP. Levels can be set for the master and for each routine.

**Q.** So what does it sound like?

<details>
<summary><b>A.</b> press REVEAL</summary>
<br>

Nobody knows. Nobody has listened to it yet.

</details>

The banner keeps the theme's time: its loop is 20 bars of 3 seconds, one minute, and she nods on every beat of it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>P199 · How this page is made</b>: a decoder, not a drawing</summary>
<br>

The banner is built the way a teletext set builds a page. The generator keeps 25 rows of 40 bytes of page memory. Bytes below 32 are the old Level 1 control codes: text colour, mosaic colour, new background, double height, flash, conceal. Each one takes up a character cell and shows as a blank, which is why every coloured word has a space in front of it and why the island has little notches where its colours change. A decoder then walks every row with the real set-at and set-after rules and turns it into cells.

```text
 row 10, cells 11 to 16, as stored          as shown
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 11  code: mosaic yellow                    a blank cell of sea
 12  mosaic: the edge of the dune           sand on sea
 13  code: new background                   a blank cell of sand
 14  code: mosaic white                     a blank cell of sand
 15  mosaic: her shorts                     white shorts on sand
 16  code: mosaic cyan                      a blank cell of sand
```

- **The picture** is drawn as 80 by 39 chunky pixels (each cell is 2 wide and 3 tall), then turned into page bytes by a small dynamic-programming search that decides where the colour codes go, one foreground and one background per cell, at the least cost to the picture.
- **The lettering** is a 5 by 9 dot-matrix font drawn for this page, smoothed on the diagonals to 10 by 18, the way the decoder chips of the day rounded their characters.
- **The colours** are the eight teletext primaries and secondaries at full strength. Nothing else.
- **The motion** is 160 pages of memory, one every half beat, decoded and diffed; every cell that changes gets a step-end opacity track. The clock is five strips of digits moved by `steps()`, and runs as a 10-hour loop from 08:00:00 to 17:59:59, because on this island it is always daytime.

One SVG, about 105 KB, no fonts, no scripts. With reduced motion set, it holds the first frame of page 100 and the clock stops.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>P800 · Island log and credits</b></summary>
<br>

The working notes, decisions and everything learned so far live in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md). The dev reel of every activity, with a heads-up display, comes from `python tools/render_demo.py --dev`, the older Python reference renderer.

```text
 P800 RAFTEXT 800                                               CREDITS
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Island .................................................... one, small
 Palm ....................................................... one, tall
 Raft ....................................................... available
 Ships seen .......................................................... 0
 Night scenes ...................................................... 0
 Page found ........................................ yes, after rolling
```

Castaway is an unofficial project inspired by the 1992 screensaver *Johnny Castaway*, which belongs to its owners; it is not affiliated with them. RAFTEXT is an invented service. The page borrows the look of broadcast teletext in general and no broadcaster's name, logo or pages; all art is original.

</details>
